title: Tiger of Mysore
summary: Tipu Sultan, also known as the Tiger of Mysore, was a ruler of the Kingdom of Mysore. He was a pioneer in the use of rocket artillery and implemented administrative innovations, including a new coinage system, calendar, and land revenue system. He fought against the British East India Company in several Anglo-Mysore Wars.

events.title: Birth of Tipu Sultan
events.description: Tipu Sultan was born in Devanahalli, near Bangalore, to Hyder Ali, a soldier in the army of the Kingdom of Mysore, and Fatima Fakhr-un-Nisa. His birth was a significant event in the growing power of Hyder Ali.

events.title: First Anglo-Mysore War
events.description: Tipu Sultan actively participated in the First Anglo-Mysore War against the British East India Company, fighting alongside his father, Hyder Ali. The war ended with the Treaty of Madras.

events.title: Second Anglo-Mysore War
events.description: Tipu Sultan played a key role in the Second Anglo-Mysore War, demonstrating his military prowess. He inflicted a major defeat on Colonel Baillie's forces at the Battle of Pollilur.

events.title: Death of Hyder Ali
events.description: Hyder Ali's death during the Second Anglo-Mysore War led to Tipu Sultan assuming control of Mysore. His succession marked a continuation of the struggle against the British East India Company.

events.title: Treaty of Mangalore
events.description: Tipu Sultan negotiated and signed the Treaty of Mangalore, ending the Second Anglo-Mysore War. The treaty restored the status quo ante bellum, with each side returning the territories they had captured.

events.title: Embassy to France
events.description: Tipu Sultan sent an embassy to Louis XVI of France, seeking an alliance against the British. This reflects Tipu's efforts to gain support from European powers to counterbalance British influence.

events.title: Third Anglo-Mysore War
events.description: The Third Anglo-Mysore War erupted due to Tipu Sultan's conflicts with Travancore, an ally of the British. The war resulted in a significant loss of territory for Mysore under the Treaty of Seringapatam.

events.title: Treaty of Seringapatam
events.description: Following the Third Anglo-Mysore War, Tipu Sultan was forced to sign the Treaty of Seringapatam. This treaty ceded roughly half of Mysore's territory to the British and their allies and also demanded a large indemnity.

events.title: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War
events.description: The Fourth Anglo-Mysore War culminated in the siege and capture of Seringapatam. Tipu Sultan died defending his capital, marking the end of the Kingdom of Mysore's independence.

events.title: Death of Tipu Sultan
events.description: Tipu Sultan was killed during the defense of Seringapatam on May 4, 1799. His death is seen as a pivotal moment in the consolidation of British power in India.
